Fight in the cause of Allah and know that Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
Whoever gives Allah a goodly loan will have it multiplied many times over, for Allah withholds and grants abundance, and to Him all return.
After Moses, the Children of Israel asked their prophet for a king to fight in Allah's way, but when fighting was prescribed most of them turned away.
Allah appoints Saul king despite objections, the chest carried by angels is his sign, and after a test at a river his few faithful soldiers pray for patience against Goliath.
They defeat Goliath's army by Allah's permission, David kills Goliath and is given kingship and prophethood, and Allah checks some people by others to keep the earth from corruption.
These are the verses of Allah recited to the Prophet in truth, and he is one of the messengers.
Allah raised some messengers above others, spoke to some and gave Jesus clear proofs, yet those after them differed and fought, some believing and some disbelieving.
Believers are told to spend from what Allah provided before a Day with no exchange, friendship or intercession.
Allah, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer: no sleep overtakes Him, none intercedes without His permission, and His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth.
There is no compulsion in religion; whoever rejects Taghut and believes in Allah holds the firmest handhold, as Allah brings believers into light and Taghut takes disbelievers into darkness.
Abraham silences King Nimrod, who argued about his Lord, by challenging him to bring the sun up from the west.
A man who asked how a ruined town could live again is made to die a hundred years and revived, and Abraham is shown how Allah revives the dead.
Spending in Allah's way is like a grain that grows seven spikes of a hundred grains each, and Allah multiplies reward for whom He wills.
Charity must not be spoiled by reminders, injury or showing off, but given from good earnings for Allah's approval, disregarding Satan's threat of poverty.
Allah gives wisdom to whom He wills, and whoever is given wisdom has been given much good.
Allah knows whatever is spent or vowed, and the wrongdoers have no helpers.
Open charity is good and secret charity to the poor better; it is for the poor restricted in Allah's cause, and those who spend night and day are rewarded.
Those who consume interest stand like one beaten into insanity by Satan; Allah permits trade and forbids interest, destroying it while increasing charities.
Those who believe, do righteous deeds, establish prayer and give zakah have their reward with their Lord, without fear or grief.
Believers must give up remaining interest or be at war with Allah and His Messenger, and if they repent they keep their principal, neither wronging nor wronged.
A debtor in hardship is given time until ease, and giving up the debt as charity is better.
Fear a Day when all are returned to Allah and every soul is paid in full for what it earned, without injustice.
Debts for a set term are written justly, witnessed by two men or a man and two women, and on a journey without a scribe a security deposit is taken.
All in the heavens and earth belongs to Allah, who will bring people to account for what they show or conceal, forgiving or punishing whom He wills.
The Messenger and the believers believe in Allah, His angels, books and messengers without distinction, and say they hear and obey and seek His forgiveness.
Allah charges no soul beyond its capacity, and the believers pray not to be blamed for forgetting or erring, nor burdened beyond their ability, but pardoned, forgiven and given victory.
The surah opens with the disjointed letters Alif, Lam, Meem.
Allah, there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence.
Allah sent down the Book in truth confirming what came before, as He revealed the Torah and the Gospel, and those who disbelieve His verses face severe punishment.
Nothing on earth or in the heaven is hidden from Allah, who forms people in the wombs as He wills; there is no deity except Him.
The Book has precise verses that are its foundation and unspecific ones the deviant follow seeking discord, while those firm in knowledge believe all of it is from their Lord.
Those of understanding pray that their hearts not deviate after guidance and that Allah grant them mercy.
They affirm that Allah will gather the people for a Day about which there is no doubt, for Allah does not fail in His promise.
The wealth and children of those who disbelieve will not avail them against Allah, and they are fuel for the Fire.
Their way is like that of Pharaoh's people and those before them, who denied Allah's signs and were seized for their sins.
Those who disbelieve are told they will be overcome and gathered to Hell, a wretched resting place.
The two armies that met at Badr, one fighting in Allah's cause and one disbelieving, are a sign and lesson that Allah supports with His victory whom He wills.
Love of women, sons, gold, silver, horses, cattle and land is made attractive, but better are gardens, purified spouses and Allah's approval for those who fear Him.
Those who fear Allah pray, saying they have believed and asking Allah to forgive their sins and protect them from the punishment of the Fire.
They are the patient, the true, the obedient, those who spend in Allah's way and those who seek forgiveness before dawn.
